title: The One Where No One Proposes

jokes.text: Joey reacts to Rachel seemingly expecting a proposal by suddenly and desperately calling out for Ross to deflect
jokes.setup: Rachel says 'I guess we should make it official, huh?' expecting something romantic
jokes.punchline: Joey panics and shouts 'Hey, Ross is here! Hey, look, it's my good friend Ross!' to escape the moment
jokes.explanation: Classic Joey panic — the moment is very character-specific. Joey's desperate, childlike deflection ('Hey, look, it's my good friend Ross!') is funny because of its transparency and his obvious terror. Strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey! Hey, hey, hey! How's it going, man? You look great! New haircut?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, Joey, I brought these flowers for Rachel and the baby.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Flowers? For me? Oh man, you shouldn't have! What's the occasion?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: They're not for you, Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh come on, don't be shy. They're beautiful. I love you, man.

jokes.text: Joey, upon receiving Ross's flowers meant for Rachel, says 'Thanks, Ross. I'm really more of a candy kind of guy.'
jokes.setup: Ross brings flowers, clearly meant for Rachel; Joey intercepts the moment
jokes.punchline: Joey treats the flowers as if they were given to him and specifies his preference for candy instead
jokes.explanation: Very Joey — the obliviousness and food-centric worldview shining through even in a romantic moment. Good economy, strong character integration. Not groundbreaking but well-executed.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I mean, Joey's been acting strange, but this is... this is a massive understatement.

jokes.text: Joey refuses to give Ross and Rachel privacy: 'Joey, could you give us a minute?' 'No.' '...What?' 'I'm sorry. I meant, No.'
jokes.setup: Ross politely asks Joey to give them privacy
jokes.punchline: Joey flat-out refuses, then corrects himself by clarifying he still means no — a non-correction
jokes.explanation: Perfectly economical joke. The beat of 'I meant, No' — where the clarification is no clarification at all — lands as a sharp double-take. Great structure: the audience expects an apology/correction and gets the same refusal restated with mock-formality. High economy score justified.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Could you give me some privacy?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm sorry, that was rude. No.

jokes.text: Jack (Rachel's dad) announces Aunt Liddy is coming, triggering the grandkids' Pavlovian response: 'Aunt Liddy's coming? That means we get $5 each!'
jokes.setup: The family announces a relative's arrival in an ostensibly warm, family reunion context
jokes.punchline: The immediate mercenary response reduces Aunt Liddy to a $5 dispenser
jokes.explanation: A quick, functional gag about family dynamics. The mercenary kid archetype is familiar. Gets a mild laugh but no surprise element.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, Aunt Ruth is coming to visit!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: That's great! You must be so excited to see her.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I am! She always gives me fifty bucks!

jokes.text: Everyone declares they need to talk to everyone else in an escalating chain: 'I need to talk to you.' 'And I need to talk to you.' 'And I need to talk to you.' — ending with 'To see if you know what these guys are talking about.'
jokes.setup: Multiple characters keep interrupting each other's urgent conversations
jokes.punchline: The final person admits they just want to find out what everyone is talking about, puncturing the drama
jokes.explanation: A structural joke playing on the crowded ensemble format. The final admission deflates the dramatic tension cleverly. Competent and functional but not especially original.

dialogue.speaker: Grandfather
dialogue.line: Watch closely as I make this coin disappear!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Dad, we've all seen that trick before.

dialogue.speaker: Grandfather
dialogue.line: Ah, but have you seen it THIS way? Now the coin is behind your ear!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wow, a coin. Behind my ear. I'm amazed. Truly.

jokes.text: Jack says Emma is 'my first grandchild' — Monica corrects him about Ben, and he backtracks: 'Well, of course, Ben. I meant my first granddaughter.'
jokes.setup: Jack gushes over Emma as his 'first grandchild', forgetting Ross's son Ben exists
jokes.punchline: He's immediately caught and awkwardly revises to 'first granddaughter,' revealing he'd simply forgotten Ben
jokes.explanation: A quick and clean character beat — Jack's social cluelessness is exposed. The lame save ('I meant granddaughter') is relatable. Competent filler-level humor.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, I want to have an important talk too!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: About what?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I don't know, but everyone else is having one, so I figured I'd jump in and see what we're all talking about.

jokes.text: Monica hears Ross planned to propose and says 'You could've done that with us there.'
jokes.setup: Ross explains he was going to have a private romantic moment with Rachel
jokes.punchline: Monica, entirely missing the point, suggests he could have proposed in front of the whole family
jokes.explanation: Monica's controlling, everything-is-a-group-activity personality lands well here. Good character integration for a brief joke.

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: Emma is my first grandchild.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Dad, what about Ben?

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: Oh right, Ben. Well, Emma is my first granddaughter.

jokes.text: Chandler says to Ross: 'You can touch yourself in front of us, but you can't talk to Rachel.'
jokes.setup: Ross wants privacy to talk to Rachel; Monica says he could've proposed in front of them
jokes.punchline: Chandler casually notes that Ross apparently doesn't mind the group seeing him touch himself in his sleep — so why is talking private?
jokes.explanation: Chandler's dry, perfectly economical delivery of a genuinely surprising line. The juxtaposition of inappropriate behavior vs. the supposedly private conversation is a smart comedic reversal. Strong economy and structure.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You're like a little old man. You like your apartment at a certain temperature, your books organized a certain way, your life planned out.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I do not!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You're like Mr. Geller.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I am nothing like Dad!

jokes.text: The reveal that Ross was touching himself in his sleep in the hospital lounge, with an Armenian family watching him instead of the TV
jokes.setup: Ross is offended by Chandler's implication about touching himself
jokes.punchline: Chandler matter-of-factly confirms it happened while he was asleep in the lounge, and the detail that an Armenian family was watching him instead of the TV escalates the humiliation
jokes.explanation: The escalating specificity — 'that Armenian family was watching you instead of the TV' — is what elevates this. It's not just the act, it's the audience and the passive displacement of actual programming. Good escalation with a sharp visual image.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I did not touch myself in front of you people!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What about last week when you were watching that nature documentary?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That was different! I was adjusting my pants!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: For forty-five minutes?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: It was a really long documentary!

jokes.text: Joey immediately pivots from the humiliating story to: 'That reminds me. That Mr. Hazmegian still has my Game Boy.'
jokes.setup: Chandler reveals the humiliating scene of Ross touching himself while an Armenian family watched
jokes.punchline: Joey's only takeaway is that he's missing a Game Boy lent to someone from that family
jokes.explanation: A beautifully Joey moment — he's completely unbothered by the disturbing revelation and only registers it as a property-recovery reminder. The specificity of the name 'Mr. Hazmegian' and the callback to the Armenian family makes this land perfectly. Strong character integration: only Joey thinks this way. Approaches the 8-anchor quality.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: A random family found it more entertaining than television.

jokes.text: Chandler responds to Joey being accidentally down on one knee with a ring: 'Again, what?' Then: 'Okay, I was down on one knee with the ring in my hand.' 'As we all are at some point during the day.'
jokes.setup: Joey explains the absurd accidental-proposal scenario
jokes.punchline: Chandler's dry 'As we all are at some point during the day' treats the outrageous situation as completely routine
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler deadpan. The absurdist pseudo-normalizing of a ridiculous scenario is his comedic signature. Economical and very quotable. The 'Again, what?' setup also lands well before the bigger punchline.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Chandler, I have to tell you something. I did something really terrible.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh my God, is this about the time you... you know?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? No!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Because we agreed never to speak of that again.

jokes.text: Chandler says about Ross: 'This is gonna kill him. You know how much he loves to propose.'
jokes.setup: Joey accidentally proposed to Rachel, stealing Ross's thunder
jokes.punchline: Chandler's deadpan observation that Ross 'loves to propose' — a sly callback to Ross's multiple failed marriages and proposals
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's sharpest lines. Chandler's dry observation works on multiple levels: it's funny in context, it's a meta-reference to Ross's entire romantic history (three marriages, numerous proposals), and it's delivered with perfect economy. 'You know how much he loves to propose' is the kind of line that gets a big laugh from fans who know the show. Strong originality in framing an old character trait as a new fresh joke.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I was on one knee with a ring.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, that's how most proposals go.

jokes.text: Chandler suggests not telling Ross, Joey agrees, then Chandler adds: 'But you have to do it before he hears about it and kicks your ass.' Joey: 'All right, let's not get carried away.'
jokes.setup: They're trying to manage the accidental proposal situation
jokes.punchline: Joey dismisses the idea that Ross could physically threaten him as an overreaction — but it's framed as if the ass-kicking is the implausible part, not the entire scenario
jokes.explanation: Joey's bravado and physical confidence are well-deployed here. Competent character joke with good economy. The reversal of priorities is amusing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, you know, with Ross's history of marriage proposals, maybe we should just treat this like one of his hobbies. Like how he collects fossils or obsesses over paleontology.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's not a hobby, Chandler, that's a lifestyle.

jokes.text: Monica tells Chandler she wants a baby; he says: 'Honey, we've been over this. I need to be facing the other way.'
jokes.setup: Monica declares 'I want a baby' in a sincere, emotional tone
jokes.punchline: Chandler interprets it as a sex request and specifies his preferred orientation — a crude but quick subversion
jokes.explanation: A quick, mildly cheeky sex joke. Lands but isn't particularly inspired. The subversion of emotional moment with a crude punchline is a well-worn formula.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Ross? Kick my ass? Please. I could take Ross with one hand tied behind my back.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, and the other hand would be tied behind his back.

jokes.text: Monica argues that having sex again will 'double their chances' of getting pregnant
jokes.setup: Chandler has redirected Monica's desire for a baby into a conversation about sex
jokes.punchline: Monica makes the technically true but hilariously clinical argument — 'it'll double our chances' — turning a romantic/emotional subject into Monica's signature optimization logic
jokes.explanation: Monica's obsessive logic is well-integrated. 'Double our chances' applies a spreadsheet mindset to conception. Competent character humor.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I want a baby.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Right now? Should I get the table out of the way?

jokes.text: Chandler: 'I think that closet's still available.'
jokes.setup: Monica and Chandler want to have sex but are in a hospital with no private space
jokes.punchline: Chandler casually suggests the hospital closet, treating a tryout location as a reasonable option — which pays off later when they're caught
jokes.explanation: A plant/setup joke that pays off when Jack catches them. The nonchalance is very Chandler. Gets rewatch value because of the later payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could we maybe just try once? I'm not saying every day, but maybe like... once a week?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Once a week? Chandler, we need to do it every day. Every other day at least!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Every day? Monica, I'm not a machine. I'm more of a... occasional appliance.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, you're going to have to become a daily appliance, because I want to get pregnant!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I know you want to get pregnant, but I also kind of want to live.

jokes.text: Monica: 'Yeah, okay, but no foreplay.' Chandler: 'Deal!'
jokes.setup: They are negotiating having sex in a hospital closet
jokes.punchline: Monica sets the terms like a business deal, and Chandler enthusiastically accepts the removal of foreplay
jokes.explanation: Monica's transactional approach to intimacy and Chandler's instant, eager agreement work together as a character double-act. 'Deal!' is the perfect economy punchline.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

jokes.text: Jack walks in on something and Monica says 'Dad, seriously!' — Jack says 'You know, you really should see someone about that.' Monica: 'Noted.'
jokes.setup: Jack has apparently witnessed something embarrassing (inferred: Monica and Chandler about to have sex or in a compromising position)
jokes.punchline: Jack treats it as a mental health matter ('you should see someone') and Monica's flat 'Noted' accepts the advice without defending herself
jokes.explanation: A quick cringe beat. Monica's 'Noted' is nice in its clipped mortification. The ambiguity of what Jack saw works for the joke. Functional but not standout.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I orchestrated the whole thing. I planted the idea in Chandler's head, I told Rachel where to be, I even convinced Phoebe to sneeze at the exact right moment so Joey would turn around. It was like conducting a symphony of romance, and I was Maestro Geller.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You didn't do any of that.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: But I could have. That's the point. I'm that good.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'I like to think of myself as the puppet master of the group.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe claims she 'talked Joey into' proposing (which is completely false and based on a misunderstanding)
jokes.punchline: She calls herself 'the puppet master of the group' with complete sincerity and self-satisfaction — entirely delusional
jokes.explanation: A great Phoebe line. The grandiosity of 'puppet master' combined with the complete wrongness of her premise is on-brand and funny. High quotability — it's a phrase that could be plucked from context. Strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Monica, you have to convince me too.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm not doing this anymore. I'm tired of being the puppet master.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'The puppet master gets tired, people.'
jokes.setup: Rachel questions the engagement; Phoebe already claimed credit for orchestrating it
jokes.punchline: Phoebe, annoyed at being questioned, leans into her self-appointed role with mock exhaustion
jokes.explanation: Extends the puppet master joke with good momentum. 'The puppet master gets tired, people' is a great line for Phoebe — regal, delusional, and oddly sympathetic. Quick callback that earns its repeat.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Joey fell asleep during the movie.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, that's not surprising. Joey sleeps like 16 hours a day.

jokes.text: Rachel asks 'Really? Even Ross?' in response to being told everyone thinks she and Joey are meant to be — meaning she's actually asking about herself and Ross
jokes.setup: Phoebe tells Rachel that everyone thinks she and 'you two' (ostensibly Rachel and Joey) are meant to be together
jokes.punchline: Rachel's 'Even Ross?' reveals she's thinking about Ross, not Joey — and Phoebe's 'Especially Ross' lands as an inadvertent truth
jokes.explanation: Nicely layered dramatic irony. The audience understands exactly what's happening while Phoebe is oblivious, and her answer 'Especially Ross' is correct for the wrong reasons. Earns rewatch bonus for the layering.

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: Wait, who's in that room? It's not me... I'm out here talking to you.

jokes.text: Rachel, referring to her supposed fiancé Joey: 'Although he does play with himself in his sleep. I can't say I'm surprised.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe calls Ross 'your fiancé' as he walks away
jokes.punchline: Rachel's addendum about the sleep habit brings back the earlier Ross revelation, but now applied to whoever she thinks is her fiancé
jokes.explanation: Good callback that adds an extra layer — Rachel's 'I can't say I'm surprised' about whoever she's marrying shows she doesn't know who proposed, while also paying off the earlier sleep habit revelation. Rewatch bonus for catching the confusion.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Wait, you mean my mom is the only thing keeping my dad from being a total creep?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, yeah. Without her, he'd be pressed against the glass at Bloomingdale's.

jokes.text: Jack walks up to a hospital room door and announces: 'There are people in there having sex.' Then: 'It can't be me. I'm standing right here.'
jokes.setup: Jack discovers Monica and Chandler in the closet having sex
jokes.punchline: His literal, almost investigative observation — 'It can't be me. I'm standing right here' — treats the situation as a logic puzzle rather than a scandal
jokes.explanation: Jack's breezy obliviousness and logical approach to discovering his daughter having sex is very funny. 'It can't be me. I'm standing right here.' is a great deadpan line — methodical and inappropriate simultaneously.

dialogue.speaker: Nurse
dialogue.line: Open up and put the breast in your mouth.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: How you doin'?

jokes.text: Jack asks Monica if she wants to 'peek' at the people having sex in the closet. Monica refuses. Jack goes anyway: 'Well, I'm peeking.'
jokes.setup: Monica is horrified; Jack doesn't understand why they shouldn't watch
jokes.punchline: Jack overrides her refusal and peeks anyway — revealing he has no sense of appropriate boundaries
jokes.explanation: Jack's total lack of decorum, contrasted with Monica's discomfort, escalates the cringe of the upcoming reveal. 'Well, I'm peeking' is a funny statement of unilateral decision-making. Rewatch bonus because the audience knows what he's about to see.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Does the baby look scared?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, the baby looks great! I mean, it's all red and wrinkly, but in a good way!

jokes.text: Jack: 'Wanna peek?' — Monica: 'No!' — Jack: 'Come on.' / Monica: 'You know what? I don't like you without Mom.' / Jack pressing: 'We're not peeking?'
jokes.setup: Jack wants to watch the strangers having sex in the hospital room
jokes.punchline: Monica's exasperated 'I don't like you without Mom' — attributing Jack's voyeurism to the absence of her mother's civilizing influence
jokes.explanation: 'I don't like you without Mom' is a genuinely great line — it captures the Monica-Jack dynamic perfectly, attributes Jack's worst behavior to the absence of his wife's control, and is quotable. The absurdity of Jack's sustained peeping interest adds to it.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa! You're gonna do WHAT in front of me?

jokes.text: Jack sees who is in the closet — Monica and Chandler — and says: 'Hello, sir. You know Monica.'
jokes.setup: Jack has peeked into the closet and seen his daughter having sex
jokes.punchline: His response is an almost formal, sociable 'Hello, sir. You know Monica.' — treating Chandler like a new acquaintance at a dinner party
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The formal introduction 'Hello, sir. You know Monica.' is a masterclass in deadpan economy. Jack has known Chandler for years — he's his son-in-law — and yet in this moment of maximum awkwardness he falls back on social-introduction register. The gap between the horror of the situation and his utterly bland courtesy is comic perfection. Easily the most quotable moment in the episode and comparable to the 8.0 anchor in its economy and character-specific absurdity.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: The baby won't take my breast. I don't know what's wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Have you tried talking to a psychiatrist? The kid might be crazy.

jokes.text: Jack wanders off to peek anyway: 'Well, I'm peeking.'
jokes.setup: Monica has refused to peek; Jack seems to concede
jokes.punchline: Jack independently decides he's peeking regardless, stated simply and without self-consciousness
jokes.explanation: Perfect button. Three words, complete comic thought. Jack's blithe resolution to do it anyway regardless of Monica's refusal is the essence of his character.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Joey's not stupid! He's actually quite intelligent.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I mean, sure, he thought the capital of France was France, but that's just one thing.

jokes.text: Joey, watching Rachel try to breastfeed: 'Dear Lord.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is trying to get Emma to breastfeed; it's a clinical but intimate scene
jokes.punchline: Joey's reverent/scandalized 'Dear Lord' — unable to process breasts in a non-sexual context
jokes.explanation: Two words, maximum character expression. Joey's involuntary reverence captures his entire personality. Very high economy score. Character integration is excellent — only Joey would react this way in this scenario.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I didn't propose to her!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, and you're not a paleontologist.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Why doesn't she want my breast?' Joey: 'I don't know! Maybe she's crazy!'
jokes.setup: Rachel is frustrated that Emma won't nurse and genuinely asks why
jokes.punchline: Joey's indignant 'Maybe she's crazy!' — defending the breast while maintaining plausible deniability that he's talking about the baby
jokes.explanation: Excellent Joey joke. The outrage in 'Maybe she's crazy!' works on two levels simultaneously — ostensibly about the baby refusing to nurse, but transparently Joey's personal offense on behalf of the breast. His character voice is completely authentic here, and the dual reading makes it genuinely clever. One of the episode's best lines. Approaches the high end of the craft scale — strong character integration comparable to the 'snip snap' anchor in specificity, though less escalatory.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You're not a real doctor.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I have a PhD in paleontology!

jokes.text: Ross assumes Phoebe's congratulations are about the baby. Phoebe says no, it's about the engagement — 'Oh, it's a secret? Goody. Yes! We haven't done the secret thing in a long time.'
jokes.setup: Ross is completely unaware of the engagement chaos; Phoebe realizes it might be a secret
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's childlike glee at having a secret — 'Goody!' — is hilariously ill-timed and self-serving
jokes.explanation: Very Phoebe — the complete disregard for the gravity of the situation replaced with excitement about the fun of a secret. 'Goody' is a funny character word choice. Good character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: A paleontologist and he can't figure out where a ring goes. Yeah, that's not gonna come back to haunt us.

jokes.text: Ross says he knew about the baby: 'Now let's give him a little credit.' Then: 'Although he did eat a piece of plastic fruit earlier.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe seems to assume Joey doesn't know about the baby
jokes.punchline: Ross defends Joey but immediately undercuts him with the plastic fruit detail, perfectly capturing Joey's specific brand of stupidity
jokes.explanation: The pivot from defending Joey to the plastic fruit is a clean setup/punchline with good economy. The detail is specific and visual enough to be funny on its own. 'Plastic fruit' as Joey's kryptonite is very believable.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I know we've lost the audience.

jokes.text: Ross: 'Now let's give him a little credit.' — immediately after: 'Although he did eat a piece of plastic fruit earlier.'
jokes.setup: Ross defends Joey's intelligence by saying surely he knows they had a baby
jokes.punchline: Immediately undercuts his own defense: 'Although he did eat a piece of plastic fruit earlier.'
jokes.explanation: Perfect self-undermining joke. The structure is excellent: defend → immediately contradict with specific evidence. 'Plastic fruit' is the right level of absurd-specific to be funny on its own, and the delivery timing ('although') is built into the script. Very well-constructed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm sorry, did that come across as not enough enthusiasm? Because I was going for 'guy who just found out his lottery ticket won fifty bucks.'

jokes.text: Phoebe asks Ross if he's lying about not proposing: 'Is this like that time you tried to convince us you were a doctor?' Ross: 'I am a doctor!'
jokes.setup: Ross denies proposing; Phoebe is skeptical
jokes.punchline: Phoebe references an apparently past incident where Ross denied being a doctor, implying his truthfulness is in question. Ross's earnest 'I AM a doctor!' is funny because it's true but sounds defensive
jokes.explanation: Funny because it implicates Ross via Phoebe's bizarre logic. 'I AM a doctor!' is a great response — true, increasingly exasperated, and somehow sounds less convincing the more emphatic it gets. Good character voice for both.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I didn't propose to her!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What do you mean you didn't propose? You proposed!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, I didn't!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Ross, we all saw you do it.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, maybe I did, but I was so tired, I don't remember doing it!

jokes.text: Chandler and Monica look at sleeping Rachel. Chandler: 'Should we wake her up?' Monica: 'No, let her sleep.' 'She's so exhausted.' Chandler: 'And so engaged.'
jokes.setup: Monica is being sweet about Rachel sleeping
jokes.punchline: Chandler's perfectly timed 'And so engaged' — wry, knowing, and cutting through the sentiment
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler: a dry comment that undercuts sentiment with perfect economy. 'And so engaged' has that Chandler rhythm — a beat that lands hard after a soft moment.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wait, did I propose? I don't remember proposing. Did I propose?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, you were on one knee.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That doesn't mean anything! I'm clumsy! I could've tripped!

jokes.text: Chandler, staring at Rachel asleep: 'Oh, my God. She thinks we're engaged!'
jokes.setup: Chandler is processing the full chaos of the situation
jokes.punchline: His delayed realization, delivered to Monica, re-centers the absurdity of the situation for the audience
jokes.explanation: More of an expository reaction beat than a joke. Functional for the plot but not particularly funny on its own.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: My father was there for all the important moments in my life. Apparently, this wasn't one of them.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'You know, Ross, doctors are supposed to be smart.'
jokes.setup: Ross says 'I didn't propose' and Phoebe presses him ('Are you lying?')
jokes.punchline: Phoebe implies Ross is too dumb to understand his own situation — the irony being that Phoebe is entirely wrong about everything
jokes.explanation: Good Phoebe irony. She's calling Ross stupid while being completely wrong herself — a double-layered comedy of errors that the audience catches. Competent character work.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wait, wait. So you're saying our sex isn't fun?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's not what I said.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, no, I heard it. It's not fun. Well, it's fun for me, but you're just lying there like it's a chore, like 'Oh, I have to go to the dentist and have sex with Chandler.'

jokes.text: Phoebe responds to Ross's explanation that he only wanted to 'start things up again' with Rachel: 'What beautiful lukewarm sentiment.'
jokes.setup: Ross explains his very modest romantic ambitions — just 'start things up again'
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's withering 'What beautiful lukewarm sentiment' perfectly names and mocks his timidity
jokes.explanation: One of the sharpest lines in the episode. 'Lukewarm sentiment' is a brilliantly precise phrase — it perfectly captures the gap between grand romantic potential and Ross's characteristically cautious, over-hedged emotional offering. The sarcasm is elegant rather than blunt. High quotability — the phrase itself is clever independent of context. Comparable to the 8.0 anchor in its economy and observational sharpness.

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: I never thought about them having sex before.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'I might be losing interest in this.'
jokes.setup: Ross is explaining the byzantine ring/proposal situation with a lot of 'no's and 'yes's
jokes.punchline: Phoebe bows out of the conversation mid-explanation — the audience surrogate admitting the situation is exhaustingly convoluted
jokes.explanation: Phoebe as audience surrogate works brilliantly here. 'I might be losing interest in this' is very economical and self-aware. It acknowledges the meta-complexity of the situation without being fully meta. High economy score.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Hey, if you guys need any help making a baby, I'm there for you.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Chandler!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? I'm just saying, I'm a giver.

jokes.text: Ross, unsure if he proposed while sleep-deprived: 'I haven't slept in 40 hours and... it does sound like something I would do.'
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to figure out if he accidentally proposed; he has no memory of it
jokes.punchline: His admission that proposing while delirious 'sounds like something I would do' — a perfectly self-aware acknowledgment of his impulsive romantic history
jokes.explanation: One of the best Ross lines of the episode. The self-awareness is funny precisely because it's true — Ross HAS a history of impulsive proposals. Character integration is excellent; this line requires the full weight of nine seasons of Ross's romantic misadventures to land at full power. 'It does sound like something I would do' is very quotable in context.

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: We've been trying to conceive, and let me tell you, the physical toll is real. I've got bruises in places I didn't know could bruise. My chiropractor asked me what happened, and I had to say, 'Well, doc, we're trying to make a baby.' He just nodded like he'd heard it a thousand times.

jokes.text: Monica and Chandler awkwardly emerge from the hospital closet after having sex; Chandler: 'Now, let's put our underwear in our pockets and walk out the door.'
jokes.setup: Monica and Chandler have had sex in a hospital closet and must now reenter civilized company
jokes.punchline: Chandler's entirely practical 'underwear in our pockets' instruction treats the situation as a solvable logistics problem
jokes.explanation: Very Chandler — finding a practical process for an embarrassing situation. 'Put our underwear in our pockets' is oddly specific and very funny as a detailed, matter-of-fact instruction. Good economy and strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could I BE any more traumatized?

jokes.text: Chandler, emerging from closet, asks Jack: 'I can still call you that, right?' (re: 'Dad')
jokes.setup: Jack has just seen Chandler having sex with his daughter; Chandler tries to manage the relationship
jokes.punchline: His anxious 'I can still call you that, right?' shows he's more worried about the social relationship than the act itself — and Jack's warm 'Of course. I'll always be your dad' normalizes the insanity
jokes.explanation: Good cringe follow-through. Chandler's social anxiety mapped onto an actually extreme situation is well-executed. Jack's warmth as counterpoint adds to the absurdity.

jokes.text: Chandler tells Jack the closet sex 'wasn't for fun' — Jack says 'It wasn't fun?' in shock, and Chandler stumbles: 'Why, why, why would you...?'
jokes.setup: Chandler is trying to explain that the sex was for procreation, not pleasure
jokes.punchline: Jack's incredulous 'It wasn't fun?' completely misses (or deliberately ignores) Chandler's point, forcing Chandler to spiral
jokes.explanation: Jack's obliviousness works consistently as a comedic engine. 'It wasn't fun?' is well-timed. The scene milks the cringe effectively.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I want to kill myself.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'Before today, I never thought of you two having sex at all. It was a simpler time.'
jokes.setup: Jack is trying to be supportive about Monica and Chandler's sex life
jokes.punchline: His wistful 'It was a simpler time' treats the moment of ignorance like a lost golden era
jokes.explanation: Beautifully economical Jack line. 'It was a simpler time' as an expression of nostalgia for not knowing your daughter has sex is a perfect articulation of parental repression. The rhythm and delivery implied by the line are excellent. High quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Monica, I need to tell you something.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, if you're about to tell me you slept with my sister again, I'm going to need to sit down. Actually, I'm already sitting. I'm going to need to lie down. Actually, I'm going to need to leave the country, fake my own death, and start a new life in a remote village where nobody knows my name or my humiliating family.

jokes.text: Jack enthusiastically tells Monica and Chandler to 'get back in there!' and offers to 'guard the door' so they can have sex again
jokes.setup: Jack learns they're trying to get pregnant
jokes.punchline: His complete reversal — from embarrassed witness to enthusiastic cheerleader/sentry — is a great escalation of his boundary-free personality
jokes.explanation: Jack's enthusiastic involvement in his daughter's sex life for procreation purposes is a funny character-driven escalation. 'I'll guard the door!' is a funny image.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: This is wrong! You barely know each other! You're not ready for marriage! You're—wait, is that a diamond?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Let me see that ring.

jokes.text: Jack asks 'Aren't you ovulating?' directly to Monica
jokes.setup: Jack is enthusiastically encouraging Monica and Chandler to have sex in the hospital
jokes.punchline: He casually references his daughter's ovulation schedule as though checking a train timetable — maximum boundary violation
jokes.explanation: The specific clinical word 'ovulating' in a father's mouth to his daughter is the joke. Very Jack. Monica's 'Daddy!' is the right straight-man response.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, Joey, this ring is beautiful!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Thanks, I got it on the show.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, it's gorgeous. You must be doing really well on 'Days of Our Lives.'

jokes.text: Jack describes his and his wife's conception attempts: 'Whenever she was ovulating, bam, we did it! That's how I got my bad hip.'
jokes.setup: Jack is recounting the vigor with which he and his wife tried to conceive
jokes.punchline: 'That's how I got my bad hip' — a TMI punchline that makes the sex both enthusiastic and physically consequential
jokes.explanation: The 'bad hip' detail is a great escalating specificity — it makes the story vividly physical in a way that's both funny and uncomfortably vivid. Good economy; the punchline is short and punchy.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Do you love Joey?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Of course I love Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, I mean do you love him love him?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I... well, I mean, he's great.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Rachel.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What? He's... he's fine.

jokes.text: Monica: 'That's funny. This conversation's how I got the bullet hole in my head.'
jokes.setup: Jack has just said his hip injury came from enthusiastic sex with Monica's mother
jokes.punchline: Monica's dark exaggeration — wishing she'd been shot rather than hear this — is a bigger, funnier response than a simple 'gross'
jokes.explanation: Monica's dark hyperbole lands well — 'bullet hole in my head' escalates the disgust to comic absurdity without being mean. Good economy; the specificity of 'bullet hole' rather than something vaguer makes it sharper. Comparable moment to 'Snip, snap' in the sense of physical consequences as a punchline structure, but lighter.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Well, I was going to tell her, but then I saw this thing on TV, and then Monica needed help moving a couch, and then I got hungry, and then... I saw a really nice pair of... you know what, I just got distracted, okay?

jokes.text: Jack begins describing the specific positions he and his wife used: 'This one time I had my knee on the sink...' Monica cuts him off: 'Daddy, I don't think we need to hear the specific positions.'
jokes.setup: Jack is already providing TMI about his sex life with Monica's mother
jokes.punchline: He begins to graphically describe a position — the 'knee on the sink' detail is visualizable enough to be horrifying — before Monica stops it
jokes.explanation: The 'knee on the sink' detail does enough work visually before Monica stops it. The interrupted-TMI structure is reliable. Functional cringe comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, you need to think about this carefully. This is serious.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So, uh... how was it?

jokes.text: Jack: 'You're right. This is about your positions.'
jokes.setup: Monica stops Jack from describing his positions with her mother
jokes.punchline: Jack completely misses her point — she wanted him to stop entirely — and redirects the conversation to their sex positions instead
jokes.explanation: Jack's oblivious pivot — hearing 'stop describing positions' as 'describe different positions' — is the comedic core of this running Jack scene. Very economical and character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey! The baby's in the way!

jokes.text: Jack: 'Although it might feel good.' Then: 'But pleasure is important, and it helps if the woman has an orgasm. You up to the task, sailor?'
jokes.setup: Jack is advising on sexual positions for conception to his son-in-law
jokes.punchline: 'You up to the task, sailor?' — Jack addressing Chandler about giving Monica an orgasm with military-style encouragement is maximum cringe comedy
jokes.explanation: 'Sailor' is a funny word choice — it imbues the conversation with an odd militaristic energy that makes the whole thing even more absurd. Jack's complete comfort with this topic is the comedic engine. Good character integration and originality in the specific phrasing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I mean, you gotta be gentle, you know? Take your time, really listen to what she wants...

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh, and then you have sex.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'Seriously, sir, my brains, all over the wall.'
jokes.setup: Jack has just asked if Chandler is 'up to the task' of giving Monica an orgasm
jokes.punchline: Chandler's dark hyperbole — matching and escalating Monica's 'bullet hole' line — implies he'd prefer to be dead rather than continue this conversation
jokes.explanation: A great callback to Monica's bullet hole line — Chandler and Monica have matching dark hyperbole responses to Jack. 'My brains, all over the wall' is very Chandler and escalates the metaphor. The callback gives the joke an extra structural point.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I wasn't confused! I knew exactly what I was doing!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay, sweetie. That's nice. Do you want some juice?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Rachel, I'm not five years old!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Of course you're not, honey. You're a big boy. A very smart big boy.

jokes.text: Joey, hearing about the engagement from Phoebe, says: 'Well, now's a good time. I'm on my way to have my ears cut off.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe says 'I need to tell you something' and it's a good time
jokes.punchline: Joey is literally on his way to have his ears cut off — an entirely random and unexplained crisis that he treats as a routine errand
jokes.explanation: Very Joey — a completely unexplained, absurd personal crisis mentioned as casually as a grocery run. 'Have my ears cut off' works because it's specific enough to be horrifying but not followed up at all. Good character integration and originality.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm just gonna grab some coffee and pretend I didn't hear any of this.

jokes.text: Phoebe, hearing Rachel said yes to Joey's proposal: 'What, are you crazy? You just had Ross' baby!'
jokes.setup: Phoebe is told Joey proposed to Rachel and she said yes
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's moral outrage focuses on the wrong thing — 'you just had Ross' baby' — rather than 'do you love Joey?'
jokes.explanation: Phoebe's confused moral calculus is funny, but the joke is fairly straightforward. Gets a laugh but isn't especially sharp.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I can't believe this is happening!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, is Chandler gonna be naked?

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'It is bigger than mine!' — referring to her Days of Our Lives storyline
jokes.setup: Phoebe is reacting to the engagement drama with increasing outrage
jokes.punchline: She makes it about her own TV storyline ('Days of Our Lives') as a point of comparison — self-referential vanity in the middle of a crisis
jokes.explanation: Phoebe's narcissistic detour to compare the drama to her soap opera storyline is a good character moment. The 'Days of Our Lives, thank you very much' self-citation is funny.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, hey, hey! You see what I did? I went over there, I told her how I felt, I made a move. That's what you gotta do, Ross.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Joey, you didn't do any of that.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, but I'm telling you about it like I did, and that's just as good.

jokes.text: Rachel explains why she'd want to marry Joey: 'Come on, I don't want to do this alone, and he's such a sweet guy. And he loves me so much.' Phoebe: 'Well, do you love him?' Rachel: 'Sure.' Phoebe: 'Sure?' Rachel: 'Yeah, I mean, whatever.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe presses Rachel on whether she actually loves Joey
jokes.punchline: 'Yeah, I mean, whatever.' — Rachel's escalating indifference to love as a criteria for marriage is both funny and sad
jokes.explanation: The escalation from 'Sure' to 'Yeah, I mean, whatever' is well-structured — each step down the caring ladder gets funnier. The audience knows exactly what's happening (she loves Ross) which adds irony. Good character writing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. I didn't propose. I was just... I had some bad shrimp earlier and I think the indigestion was making me say crazy things.

jokes.text: Rachel, after admitting she doesn't want to marry Joey: 'Could you be a dear and go tell him?'
jokes.setup: Rachel has just realized she doesn't want to marry Joey
jokes.punchline: Instead of going to tell him herself, she casually asks Phoebe to do it — with the breezy social register of asking someone to fetch a coffee
jokes.explanation: Rachel's pampered, princess-y personality is well-deployed here. 'Could you be a dear and go tell him?' is very funny in its breezy casualness about a devastating task. Good economy and character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So what you're saying is, you don't want to rush into anything, but you've already slept with her?

jokes.text: Joey explains why he didn't tell Rachel about the accidental proposal: 'She had the ring on, she seemed so excited, and then she took her breast out.'
jokes.setup: Chandler asks why Joey didn't correct Rachel's misunderstanding
jokes.punchline: Joey lists three reasons — the ring, the excitement, and then the breast — with the breast as the clincher that derailed his plans entirely
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The list structure ('the ring... the excitement... and then she took her breast out') builds perfectly, with the breast as the punchline/final obstacle. The structure implies that Joey had noble intentions but was physically incapacitated by the nursing. Completely authentic to Joey's character — he's not a bad person, he's just Joey. Very quotable. The callback to the breastfeeding scenes gives it additional structural weight. Comparable to the 8.0 anchor in its economy and character-specific absurdity.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm really sorry. I mean it. I was wrong and I—

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa! Is that... are you...? Oh my God, that's amazing!

jokes.text: Chandler: 'And what did it look like?' Joey: 'I didn't look at it. The stupid baby's head was blocking most of it.'
jokes.setup: Chandler asks Joey what the breast looked like
jokes.punchline: Joey's frustrated complaint that the baby's head was 'blocking most of it' — aggrieved that an infant had the audacity to obstruct his view
jokes.explanation: Possibly the funniest Joey joke in the episode. 'The stupid baby's head was blocking most of it' is a perfect articulation of Joey's id — he's annoyed at a newborn for being in the way. The indignation in 'stupid baby's head' is entirely authentic and entirely wrong. Maximum character integration. The structure (Chandler's straight-man question + Joey's answer) is clean and economic. High quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: Hey, remember those pregnancy pamphlets I brought? Well, I need you to go get them from my bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Other character
dialogue.line: Now? We're in the middle of something!

dialogue.speaker: Jack
dialogue.line: I know, I know, but I really need them right now.

jokes.text: Joey, leaving, casually mentions to Chandler: 'By the way, two people screwing in there if you want to check that out.'
jokes.setup: Joey is leaving to talk to Rachel and seems to be in a serious emotional moment
jokes.punchline: He helpfully tips Chandler off about the in-progress sex in the closet as though sharing a restaurant recommendation
jokes.explanation: Perfect Joey delivery — the throwaway nature of this tip is what makes it so funny. He's completely unbothered, just doing a friendly heads-up. 'If you want to check that out' is a generous framing, as though he's sharing a hot tip. Very high economy. The callback to the closet sex scene adds another layer.

jokes.text: Ross to sleeping Rachel: 'I didn't propose to you.' (Rachel sleepily misattributing) 'You didn't propose to me. Joey did.' Ross: 'Poor baby, you're so tired.'
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to have a serious conversation with an exhausted, confused Rachel
jokes.punchline: Rachel correctly names Joey as the proposer, but Ross interprets it as sleep-delirious confusion and pats her head — the audience knows she's right, he doesn't
jokes.explanation: A great dramatic irony beat. Rachel accidentally tells the truth; Ross dismisses it as delirium. 'Poor baby, you're so tired' is condescending in a funny way — he's wrong, she's right. The scene structure is excellent for this type of situation-comedy confusion.

jokes.text: Joey, confronted about proposing, says 'No.' Rachel: 'Yes, you did.' Joey: 'Actually, technically, I didn't.'
jokes.setup: Everyone is trying to untangle who proposed and what happened
jokes.punchline: 'Actually, technically, I didn't' — Joey splitting hairs on the technicality of an accidental proposal
jokes.explanation: Joey's legalistic distinction is funny given his usual anti-sophistication. 'Technically, I didn't' is a decent line. Competent but not exceptional.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Yeah, but you said, 'Will you marry me?' Joey: 'No, I didn't.' Rachel: 'Yes, you did.' Joey: 'No, I didn't.' Rachel: 'Yes, you did. Oh, my God, you didn't.'
jokes.setup: Joey and Rachel are going back and forth on whether he said 'Will you marry me?'
jokes.punchline: Rachel has a mid-argument epiphany — she realizes he didn't say it, mid-'yes-you-did' — the self-correction while arguing is the joke
jokes.explanation: The mid-sentence reversal — 'Yes, you did. Oh, my God, you didn't.' — is very well-structured. The audience is waiting for the other shoe to drop and it comes at exactly the right moment. Good comedic escalation and structure.

jokes.text: Rachel asks why Joey didn't tell her sooner. Joey: 'Well, I tried, but people kept coming in, and then you took your breast out.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is demanding to know why Joey let this confusion go on
jokes.punchline: The breast excuse returns as a callback — again, the breast as an insurmountable obstacle to Joey's good intentions
jokes.explanation: The callback to 'and then you took your breast out' earns its repeat — it's established as Joey's official excuse now, and re-deploying it confirms it as a running character trait. Good economy and character integration.

jokes.text: Ross: 'You saw her breast?' Joey: 'I'll tell you about it later. Be cool.'
jokes.setup: Joey mentions that Rachel took her breast out in his presence
jokes.punchline: Joey's nonchalant 'I'll tell you about it later. Be cool.' — treating a glimpse of Rachel's breast like a hot gossip item he'll debrief Ross on
jokes.explanation: One of the most Joey sentences ever spoken. 'I'll tell you about it later. Be cool.' is perfect character voice — conspiratorial, excited, and completely inappropriate given that it's Ross's baby mama's breast and they're in the middle of a crisis. Very high economy and character integration. Highly quotable.

jokes.text: Joey, in the confrontation scene: 'That's right. There's a lot going on here, and I think I ate some bad fruit earlier.'
jokes.setup: Everyone is simultaneously realizing the tangled engagement misunderstanding
jokes.punchline: Joey exits the emotional confrontation to revisit the plastic fruit incident — his stomach is his truest concern
jokes.explanation: The callback to the plastic fruit is funny and very Joey — returning to his physical self-concern in the middle of an emotionally heavy moment. 'Bad fruit' as his primary anxiety is perfect character voice. Good economy.

jokes.text: Joey, to Ross who's reluctant to rush into a relationship with Rachel: 'Yeah, dude, I totally understand. Usually after I have a baby with a woman, I like to slow things down!'
jokes.setup: Ross says he doesn't want to rush into anything with Rachel
jokes.punchline: Joey's faux-understanding agreement, which immediately reveals the absurdity of Ross's position — having a baby with someone and 'slowing things down' is a ridiculous concept
jokes.explanation: Joey's unexpected sharpness here is what makes this special. He usually doesn't land the insightful observation, so when he does it hits harder. 'Usually after I have a baby with a woman, I like to slow things down' perfectly exposes the absurdity of Ross's position with an ironic reversal. Well-structured and economical. One of the stronger jokes in the episode.

jokes.text: Ross and Rachel are having a soft romantic reconnection moment — building back toward each other — when Ross notices: 'You're wearing the ring.'
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel are finally having a genuine, heartfelt conversation
jokes.punchline: Ross notices Rachel is still wearing the engagement ring — which derails the moment and raises new questions
jokes.explanation: More of a plot beat than a joke — the comedic element is the interruption of the romantic moment. Gets a mild laugh of recognition. Functional but not particularly crafted as a comedy moment.

jokes.text: Ross piecing together that Rachel said yes to Joey: 'And you told Phoebe you were engaged.' ... 'When you thought Joey proposed... did you say yes?'
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel's romantic reconnection keeps being interrupted by new revelations
jokes.punchline: Ross's dawning realization — the audience sees his face fall as he processes that Rachel said yes to Joey — is a reaction beat that's played for maximum cringe
jokes.explanation: The punchline here is structural — the audience knows what's coming before Ross does, so when he gets there, the cringe is earned. Stronger as a dramatic irony beat than as a pure joke.

jokes.text: Jack walks in on the tender Ross/Rachel moment with pamphlets: 'Kids, I spoke to a doctor and picked up these pamphlets on how to get pregnant.' Then realizes he's interrupting and quickly retreats to retrieve his pamphlets.
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel have a charged, awkward romantic moment in the wake of the engagement chaos
jokes.punchline: Jack completely disrupts it with cheerful pamphlets about pregnancy — and then, embarrassed, comes back for them
jokes.explanation: Jack's oblivious intrusion is a great episode-capper. The beat of him retrieving the pamphlets — mortified but still needing them — is a lovely bit of physical comedy and character consistency. The running gag of Jack's total lack of boundaries lands as a satisfying final note. Good structure for a closing scene.

tmdb_overview: Following Rachel's acceptance of Joey's accidental proposal, confusion reigns as Rachel wonders whether it was the right thing to do and Phoebe can't seem to mind her own business. Finally, Rachel, Ross and Joey get together and figure out that no one was actually going to propose. Meanwhile, Mr. Geller walks in on Monica and Chandler having sex in a closet.
insight: Season premiere delivers steady laughs with character-driven cringe, 58 jokes in 19 minutes.
